category_title: Adolescents positioned as struggling readers who resist institutional labels
minimal_context: Angelica is at a bookstore with her reading teacher to select books for independent reading.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We have some time in the bookstore today. Go ahead and pick out some books to read independently for class.

STUDENT: Great, it's another reading class. I saw all these books and I just thought this is going to be really boring.

TUTOR: Why don't you look at the books in this series over here?

STUDENT: (Reads the back cover) This looks like this is not my type and I really don't care for this one. I've never really been interested in those books. They just look boring to me.

TUTOR: Just pick out some books that you would probably like.

STUDENT: You're really going to buy me some books? I'm probably not even going to read them.

options.A: Cue Angelica to evaluate her performance of targeted behaviors using a self-management system while browsing the bookstore.
options.B: Set up stations around the bookstore corresponding to different ages, placing artifacts and books typical of those ages to aid Angelica's memory.
options.C: Ask, 'Why? Why do you think that?' to prompt justification from Angelica regarding her thoughts on the books.
options.D: Provide immediate and instructional feedback, helping Angelica to understand what she should have done during the bookstore visit.
